note.text:
We count years from the year given as the birth of Jesus Christ.
• Years before it are BC (Before Christ). They count backwards: 500 BC is earlier than 200 BC.
• Years after it are AD (Anno Domini, “in the year of the Lord”): AD 476, AD 2026.
• There is no year 0: 1 BC is followed by AD 1.
Years between two dates: if both are AD or both BC, subtract. If one is BC and one is AD, add them and take away 1 (no year 0).
Centuries: a century is 100 years. AD 1 to AD 100 is the 1st century; 1801 to 1900 is the 19th century; we live in the 21st century. So 1884 is in the 19th century, one more than its first two figures.
Some books write BCE and CE instead of BC and AD.

worked_example.problem: How many years are there from {year(a)} to {year(b)}?
steps: One date is BC and the other AD: add them.
There is no year zero, so take away one: {b - a} − {1} = {yearsBetween(a, b)}.

cards.idea: BC years count backwards: the bigger the number, the earlier the year.

misconceptions.explain: BC years count backwards: the bigger number is further back in time.

cards.idea: Between two AD dates, or two BC dates, subtract to find the years between them.
There is no year zero. From a BC date to an AD date: add the two numbers, then take away one.

misconceptions.explain: There is no year 0: 1 BC is followed by AD 1.
That is the year before 1 BC, not after.

cards.idea: A century is a hundred years. A year is in the century one more than its hundreds: {year(e)} is in the {century(e)}.

questions.prompt: How many years are there from {year(a)} to {year(b)}?

misconceptions.explain: Both dates are AD: subtract the earlier from the later.
The century is one more than the hundreds: 1884 is in the 19th century.
This is an AD year, so the century is AD.
Add only one to the hundreds.

solution: {year(y)} has {floor(y / 100)} full hundred{floor(y / 100) == 1 ? '' : 's'} and some more years.
So it is in the next century: {answer}.

misconceptions.explain: BC dates come before all AD dates, and among BC dates the bigger number is earlier.

solution: {a < 0 && b < 0 ? 'Both are BC: the bigger number is earlier.' : 'A BC date is earlier than any AD date.'}

questions.prompt: How many years are there from {year(-a)} to {year(-(a - d))}?

misconceptions.explain: Both dates are BC: subtract the smaller number from the bigger.

questions.prompt: How many years are there from {year(-a)} to {year(b)}?

misconceptions.explain: There is no year 0: add the two numbers, then take away 1.
One date is BC and one is AD: add the two numbers (then take away 1).

solution: One date is BC and one is AD: add. {a} + {b} = {a + b}.

questions.prompt: On the timeline, how many years are there from event A to event B?

misconceptions.explain: Count across BC and AD: add, then take away 1, because there is no year 0.

solution: A is at {year(p * 50)} and B is at {year(q * 50)}.
